prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your ZIP code, budget, house size, whether you have ductwork, brand preferences, and whether you want a high-efficiency system or a basic replacement. I can help find good options if you tell me your ZIP code and a few details. Meanwhile, here’s a practical guide to choose a top installer in Atlanta.

Quick questions so I can recommend specific companies:
- ZIP code or neighborhood
- Single-family home or multi‑unit / commercial?
- Rough square footage and number of rooms
- Do you have ducted central air now (replacement) or is this a new install?
- Any brand preferences (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Rheem, Goodman, etc.)?
- Budget range or need for financing?
- Timeline for replacement (ASAP vs. flexible)?

How to pick the best contractor (checklist)
1. Licensing & insurance
   - Confirm they’re licensed to do HVAC work in Georgia and carry liability insurance and workers’ comp.
2. Certifications
   - Look for NATE-certified technicians and EPA 608 certification for refrigerant handling.
3. Written, itemized estimates
   - Get at least 3 written bids that list equipment model numbers, SEER rating, capacity (tons), labor, permit fees, and any required ductwork or electrical work.
4. Proper sizing & design
   - Insist on a Manual J load calculation and ductwork/airflow inspection (not just “rule-of-thumb” sizing).
5. Efficiency & equipment options
   - Compare SEER ratings, heat-pump vs. straight AC, sound ratings, and manufacturer warranties.
6. Permits & code compliance
   - Installer should obtain all permits and pull inspections as required by local code.
7. Warranties & service
   - Clarify manufacturer warranty and what the installer’s labor warranty covers (and for how long).
8. Local reputation & reviews
   - Check Google/Yelp, Better Business Bureau, Angi, and neighborhood Facebook/Nextdoor for recent experiences.
9. Ask about rebates & financing
   - See if they help you capture utility rebates, tax credits, or offer 0% financing.
10. Red flags
   - Extremely low bids, pressure to sign immediately, no written estimate, unwillingness to pull permits, or poor online reviews about workmanship or follow-up.

Questions to ask each contractor
- “Will you perform a Manual J load calc and provide the report?”
- “Which exact model are you recommending and why?”
- “What is included in the price (permit, disposal of old unit, start-up, refrigerant, labor warranty)?”
- “Who services the unit under warranty — you or the manufacturer?”
- “Can you provide recent references in my neighborhood?”

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and a couple of the items above and I’ll prepare a short list of highly-reviewed Atlanta installers to contact and a comparison checklist you can use when getting estimates.
